description: Detects PowerShell execution using the EncodedCommand parameter (Base64), frequently used to hide malicious scripts.
Detects PowerShell commands followed immediately by suspicious characters, paths, or flags, indicating non-interactive execution.
Detects PowerShell `Invoke-Expression` (IEX) or `Invoke-WebRequest` calls, common methods for executing memory-resident code or downloading payloads.
Detects the 'Download and Execute' pattern where content from `curl` or `wget` is piped directly into a shell or script interpreter.
Detects `mshta.exe` (a Living-off-the-Land binary) executing remote HTA files or inline scripts (VBScript/JScript).
Detects misuse of Windows utility binaries (`certutil`, `bitsadmin`) to download files, decode payloads, or modify certificate stores.
Detects `rundll32.exe` executing JavaScript code directly via the command line.
Detects a specific chain of commands: CMD starting a hidden PowerShell process to download a file and immediately execute it.
Detects social engineering bait text often associated with 'Fake CAPTCHA' clipboard injection attacks.
Detects `Invoke-Expression` attempting to execute a string derived specifically from `FromBase64String`.
Detects PowerShell using the .NET `WebClient` class to download files or strings, bypassing standard cmdlets like `Invoke-WebRequest`.
Detects PowerShell format operator obfuscation (e.g., `& ('{0}{1}' -f 'I','EX')`), used to hide command signatures.
Detects Base64 decoded content being piped directly into a shell or interpreter, widely used to obfuscate payload content.
Detects macOS AppleScript (`osascript`) executing shell commands, a bridge often used by malware to access system functions.
Detects malicious processes detached from the terminal using `nohup`, intended to persist after the user closes the window.
Detects attempts to remove the 'com.apple.quarantine' attribute (Gatekeeper) on macOS to bypass security warnings.
Detects `dscl` commands checking for valid credentials locally, often used by credential stealers to validate captured passwords.
Detects the specific 'one-liner' pattern used to inject a new job into the user's crontab for persistence without opening an editor.
Detects the creation or modification of Windows Scheduled Tasks, a common technique for establishing persistence.
Detects the 'Download and Execute' pattern where Invoke-WebRequest retrieves a payload via the -Uri parameter and Start-Process immediately executes it.
Detects the PowerShell download cradle where irm/iwr output is piped into iex, the classic ClickFix clipboard payload shape.
Detects iex executing a Net.WebClient download directly, without a preceding powershell keyword.
Detects `msiexec.exe` being invoked to fetch and install a remote package directly over HTTP/HTTPS, commonly abused in ClickFix and malvertising lures.
Detects in-memory extraction and execution of zipped payloads via .NET ZipArchive and WebClient without writing the archive to disk.
Detects PowerShell payloads using P/Invoke to hide console windows (ShowWindow 0) combined with download-and-execute activity.
Detects mounting remote WebDAV shares over HTTP/HTTPS using `net use` to stage and execute remote binaries or scripts.
Detects command substitution execution where `curl` or `wget` output is evaluated directly inside a shell `-c` subshell (e.g., bash -c "$(curl ...)").
Detects `conhost.exe` spawned with `--headless` to execute background command prompts and avoid spawning visible interactive terminal windows.
Detects CMD execution with delayed environment expansion (`/v:on`) and dynamic variable concatenation (`!var!`) used to assemble and run obfuscated commands.
Detects PowerShell cradles fetching payloads hosted on public CDN mirrors (such as jsDelivr) often abused to host staging scripts.
Detects inline P/Invoke definitions targeting `ShowWindow` or `GetConsoleWindow` to minimize/hide the current console right before file download or extraction.
Detects PowerShell unzipping an archive via `Expand-Archive` followed by process execution using `Start-Process`.
Detects native `tar.exe` being invoked to unpack staging archives (e.g., downloaded via curl) on modern Windows systems.
Detects process creation using the .NET WMI accelerator `[wmiclass]'Win32_Process'` to evade standard `Start-Process` and `cmd.exe` command-line monitoring.
Detects the Windows `finger.exe` utility invoked inside a CMD `for /f` loop to download and execute remote payloads via TCP port 79.
Detects command pipeline execution where downloaded content is directly piped into `cmd.exe` or macOS `osascript -l JavaScript`.
Detects fake authentication errors, CAPTCHA bypass lures, and 'Press Enter' user prompts commonly embedded in ClickFix clipboard injection chains.
Detects chained PowerShell pipeline operator expressions (`|&('%'){...}`) used to construct deeply obfuscated script execution wrappers.
Detects execution of script blocks created dynamically from file contents using Get-Content (-Raw) and .Invoke(), bypassing script-file execution policies.
Detects Bash here-string execution (`<<<`) evaluating Base64-decoded command substitution strings directly in memory.
Detects PowerShell web cradles utilizing quote-interruption obfuscation within domain names or paths (e.g., c"d"n.jsdelivr) piped to IEX.
Detects msiexec execution abusing custom installer properties (e.g., S1=) populated with Cyrillic homoglyphs and ClickFix 'press Enter to verify' bait strings.
Detects command-line switch evasion against msiexec using Unicode superscript or phonetic homoglyphs (such as /ᵖᵃᶜᵏᵃᵍᵉ) to bypass ASCII flag checks.
Detects mounting a remote WebDAV share over HTTP via an IP address followed immediately by inline execution of a staged script on the mapped drive.
Detects malicious batch discovery scanning Google Chrome cache structures for specific payload file sizes to carve out and execute dropped VBScript files.
Detects in-memory AMSI (Antimalware Scan Interface) bypass attempts manipulating `amsiInitFailed` via .NET reflection.
Detects Windows Console Host (`conhost.exe`) spawned in `--headless` mode chaining shell interpreters to conceal child process windows.
Detects download cradles connecting to hosts designated via integer/DWORD/decimal IP representations (e.g., http://1614733393/) to evade standard IP-pattern detection.

description: Detects terminal-based fake verification lures that print simulated Cloudflare or anti-bot verification milestones in console output.
Detects execution of PowerShell download cradles wrapped directly inside `& ([scriptblock]::Create((irm ...)))` constructs without piping to IEX.
Detects macOS/BSD-style Base64 decoding (`base64 -D`) generating dynamic URLs for `curl` piped directly into execution shells.
Detects abuse of Windows Package Manager (`winget`) to silently install DenoLand.Deno and immediately run remote, unrestricted scripts via `deno run -A`.
Detects rapid run-key persistence established via PowerShell `Set-ItemProperty` (`sp`) pointing to dynamically created or unzipped scripts.
Detects `Invoke-Command` executing Unicode Base64-decoded script blocks in memory without writing files to disk.

source: navigator\.clipboard\.writeText\b[\s\S]{1,600}?(?:Press the Windows Key|CTRL \+ V|reCAPTCHA Verification ID)
description: Detects web clipboard injection logic that forces malicious CLI payloads into the user's clipboard alongside step-by-step Run-dialogue lure instructions.
